comment: The Ministry supports the statement that requirements should be expressed testably so that countries can validate conformance, including the claims of suppliers, before and during procurement. We would add that this is materially easier where the artefacts against which conformance is tested are national assets rather than supplier deliverables. Slovenia requires suppliers to publish archetypes, templates, profiles, terminology bindings, implementation guides and validation rules to a repository designated by the Ministry, as a condition of acceptance. The guidance would be strengthened by naming publication of conformance artefacts as a procurement condition rather than a technical practice.
